audit_result.proof_trace: `setAcceptedCapital` (L436-442) stores the caller-supplied `merkleRoot` directly into `s_saleStatus.acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot` with no `!= bytes32(0)` guard; passing zero is syntactically valid. When the root is zero, `_verifyCanClaimExcessCapital` (L767) always fails `MerkleProofLib.verify` (no leaf hash can equal 0), reverting every `withdrawExcessInvestedCapital` call with a misleading `CannotWithdrawExcessInvestedCapital` error and DoSing excess-capital withdrawal for all investors.
audit_result.attack_scenario: A Legion admin (or a compromised Legion key) calls `setAcceptedCapital(bytes32(0))`; all subsequent `withdrawExcessInvestedCapital` calls revert at the Merkle check, locking investors' entitled excess capital until the root is explicitly corrected — during which any time-bounded refund window may expire.

PROP-legion-backe-inv-023.text: OpenApp setAcceptedCapital Merkle root must not be zero when used for excess withdrawal.
